subject: physics
title: Internal energy
key_idea: Internal energy is the total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles in a system. Heating increases it. This either raises the temperature or produces a change of state.

blocks.text: A system stores energy inside it, in its particles (atoms and molecules). This is its internal energy.

items.meaning: The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles that make up a system.
The energy a particle has because it is moving. Faster particles have more.
The energy stored in the particles because of the forces between them and how far apart they are.

items: The temperature of a substance depends on the average kinetic energy of its particles.
Changes in potential energy do not change the temperature.
Heating a system increases the energy of its particles, so its internal energy increases.
Cooling a system decreases the energy of its particles.
Internal energy = total kinetic energy + total potential energy of all the particles.
Faster particles mean more kinetic energy and a higher temperature.

blocks.text: Heating a system changes the energy stored in it. There are two possible results.

items: The temperature rises. The particles move faster, so their kinetic energy increases.
There is a change of state. The temperature stays constant. The potential energy of the particles increases and their kinetic energy does not change.

diagram.alt: Temperature against time as a block of ice is heated until it melts, the water warms, boils and becomes steam. The line is flat while the ice melts and while the water boils.

items: On the sloping parts, energy raises the kinetic energy of the particles.
On the flat parts, energy increases the potential energy. The particles are pulled apart against the forces between them.
Heating by an electric heater transfers energy to the thermal energy store of the heater and then of the water.

diagram.alt: Sort each change into kinetic energy changing or potential energy changing.
diagram.prompt: Which energy of the particles changes? Sort each example.

items.text: Air in a balloon cools down
A metal block is heated from 20 °C to 50 °C

items: Heating either raises the temperature or changes the state.
Temperature rises: the kinetic energy of the particles increases.
Change of state: the potential energy increases and the temperature is constant.

checks.q: What is meant by internal energy?
checks.a: The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles that make up the system.

checks.q: Ice at 0 °C is melting. What happens to the kinetic energy and the potential energy of its particles?
checks.a: The kinetic energy stays the same, because the temperature is constant. The potential energy increases.

checks.q: Explain how the internal energy of water changes as it is heated from 20 °C to 25 °C.
checks.a: The mean kinetic energy of the particles increases, which increases the internal energy of the water.

worked_example.question: A scientist poured some liquid nitrogen into a container. The container was then sealed. Explain how the internal energy of the nitrogen changed as the nitrogen turned from a liquid to a gas.
answer_points: the potential energy of the particles increases
but the kinetic energy of the particles does not change, as the temperature does not change
worked_example.tip: The third mark depends on the first two.

worked_example.question: A vaccine is a solid. Its temperature is first raised to its melting point, but it remains as a solid. Explain two reasons why more energy is needed to change the solid vaccine into a liquid at its melting point.
answer_points: energy is needed to change the state of a material
energy is needed to break or weaken the bonds between the molecules (overcome the attractive forces between the solid molecules)
or: some heat transfer with the surroundings or the container
worked_example.tip: Any two of these points score. Energy needed to increase the separation of the molecules is also allowed.

worked_example.question: The temperature of the water in a beaker decreases. State what happens to the internal energy of the water. Describe the change in terms of the energy of the particles.
answer_points: The (average) kinetic energy of the particles decreases

worked_example.question: Liquid nitrogen warms up and changes state from a liquid into a gas. Describe the changes to the arrangement and motion of particles when the liquid nitrogen changes state.
answer_points: The particles are much further apart
The particles move with a much higher speed (higher kinetic energy)
